angle: Earlier same-node 6-arm ablation (2026-08-25, outputs/arm_bf16 and outputs/arm_nvfp4_deq) as a control for the 4+4 long runs: step count, lr schedule, prompt pairing, step-for-step reward comparison over steps 1-10, what its write-up concluded, and what differs between ablation and long runs (schedule, topology, code commits).
summary: The control does NOT show that something changed: the BF16-over-NVFP4 reward gap in the long runs is already present, in the same direction and about the same size, in the 10-step same-node ablation on the identical prompts, and it is present at step 1 before any optimizer update. Facts: (1) The ablation ran exactly 10 steps per arm (ablation_arms.py:100 num_training_steps=10, :116 lr_scheduler.total_steps=10) with warmup 2 + linear decay: trainer/lr = 5e-7, 1e-6, 1e-6, 8.75e-7 ... 1.25e-7 at step 10 (mean 6.0e-7 over steps 1-10); the long runs use 5e-7, 1e-6, then constant 1e-6 (mean 9.5e-7). (2) All four runs consumed the same 8 prompts at every policy version 0-9 (8/8 prompt-text md5 overlap; rollout/prompt_length/mean identical at steps 1-10 in all 11 output dirs), while the sampled responses differ (0/16 and 1/16 shared response hashes at pv0), so ablation and long runs are independent replicates on identical prompts. (3) Steps 1-10 rollout reward: ablation BF16 0.0984 vs NVFP4 0.0641 (paired sign 8+/1=/1-, mean gap +0.034); long BF16 0.0813 vs NVFP4 0.0672 (7+/1=/2-, +0.014). The NVFP4 arm reproduces itself across code versions almost step-for-step (4/10 steps identical values, mean diff -0.003), as do its mismatch metrics: logprob diff mean -0.00280 (ablation) vs -0.00272 (long), clip fraction 0.0199 vs 0.0204, zero-std fraction 0.74 vs 0.75 (BF16: 0.66 / 0.70). (4) At step 1 (policy version 0 = untouched HF weights, so only rollout-side expert precision differs) BF16 scored 6/64 and 5/64 while four independent NVFP4-deq replicates (arm_nvfp4_deq, arm_nvfp4_deq_4x4, arm_nvfp4_deq_4x4_100, arm_nvfp4_deq_4x4_long) scored 2/64, 4/64, 3/64, 2/64: pooled 0.086 vs 0.043, one-sided Fisher p=0.073. Over steps 1-10 all four NVFP4-deq replicates (0.0641/0.0703/0.0578/0.0672) lie below both BF16 replicates (0.0984/0.0813), ratio 0.72, P=0.067 under exchangeability; the other low-precision arms sit in between (mxfp8_hp 0.083, mxfp8_deq 0.075, mxfp8_e2e 0.073, nvfp4_hp 0.073). (5) In the long runs the gap is present from the first block (1-10: 0.081/0.067; 11-20: 0.102/0.052; 21-30: 0.156/0.105; 1-30: 0.113/0.075), so the PR draft's "within noise for the first ~30 steps" is not supported by block means. (6) The ablation write-up (repos/titan-nvfp4 nvfp4_4over6_results/README.md, commit 1f47dc8c5 2026-08-25) reports reward mean 0.098 (bf16) vs 0.064 (nvfp4_deq, lowest of six arms) but concludes "Loss/reward/grad-norm/entropy show no precision ordering" and "Ten steps at lr 1e-6 is a short horizon — this is a stability/parity smoke, not a convergence claim"; it also documents the step-3 all-zero-reward no-op in arm_nvfp4_deq, which the long NVFP4 run reproduces exactly (step 3 reward 0, grad norm 0) while both BF16 runs got 1/64. (7) Differences ablation vs long: lr decay-to-0-at-10 vs constant 1e-6; 10 vs 300+ steps; same-node 2+2 (trainer dp_shard1/tp2/ep2, generator tp2/ep2, gb-nvl-118) vs cross-node 4+4 (trainer dp_shard2/tp2/ep4, generator dp2/tp2/ep4, torchstore NCCL/MNNVL sync, 8 h windows with 1-2 replayed steps per handoff); AIME validation at steps 0/10 vs none; model-only vs full checkpoints; code titan 28426e01d(+uncommitted run-local patches)/ao 3c9fbc59a on 08-25 vs titan a24a9e08e/ao 2f6cf4fce on 09-05 (recipe-selector consolidation, torchao grouped-GEMM dispatcher wiring, skip knob; nvfp4.py 224 lines and four_over_six_grouped.py 36 lines changed), same container image, fa/DSL overlays and FOUR_OVER_SIX_GROUPED_ROW_SCALED_FUSED_BF16_OUT=1 in both launchers; the long runs did not use the experimental inference weight cache branch. Interpretation: the gap is intrinsic to the NVFP4-deq arm at this base model and workload and is not created by the constant-lr schedule, the cross-node topology, the prompt stream, or the Aug-30 code refactor; the ablation simply lacked horizon and replicates and its write-up under-read a -35% reward difference. The step-1 evidence points to an inference-side penalty (the NVFP4-quantized policy solves fewer DAPO-math prompts before any training), which then leaves GRPO with fewer non-degenerate groups; whether NVFP4 additionally learns less per unit of signal, and whether a different lr would let it climb later, cannot be decided from this angle.

KEY TIMING FACT: the gap is NOT a later divergence of two initially-equal curves. NVFP4 is below BF16 from the first 20 steps (0.059 vs 0.091; paired t over steps 1-20 = +3.70, BF16 higher on 17/20; steps 1-30 t=+4.15, 24/30, 217 vs 143 correct of 1920 samples) while lr is 1e-6 and the policy has barely moved; the difference then GROWS because BF16 improves (slope +0.063/100 steps, t=9.7) and NVFP4 does not (+0.0076/100, t=1.8; zero-std slope -0.011/100, t=-1.0). Conditional on prompt difficulty (BF16 reward bin), NVFP4 achieves 0.60-0.72x of BF16 in steps 1-100 and 0.33-0.43x in 201-300 (OLS nvfp4=0.547*bf16+0.011 early, 0.385*bf16-0.005 late). Cross-run per-step reward r=0.675 (lag +/-1: 0.04/-0.02, lag 5: 0.02; detrended 0.72) confirms shared prompt difficulty drives ~45% of per-step variance. HANDOFFS: no resume artefacts -- replayed steps (14 BF16, 13 NVFP4 pairs at identical weights+prompts) differ by std 0.043 (sampling-noise floor), lr/policy_version/prompt_length identical across the pair, 5-step before/after means at all 11 handoffs move within that floor, first-3-steps-after-resume reward/logprob-diff/clip means match the rest (NVFP4 0.073 vs 0.089 reward, n=21; -0.00289 vs -0.00291 lpd). INTERPRETATION: the tfevents evidence points to a deficit that exists at (near-)identical weights, i.e. the quantized 4over6 forward used by BOTH the vLLM generator and the trainer (shared model_spec, config_registry.py:798-803) lowers the sampled-response accuracy of Qwen3-30B-A3B on DAPO-math before any RL signal, and the resulting 30% fewer signal-carrying groups (2.3-2.4 vs 2.9->4.1 per step) plus 4-6x larger trainer/generator mismatch are consistent with slower or stalled learning; the sweep cannot separate 'quantized rollout policy is weaker' from 'quantized trainer gradient is worse' -- that needs an off-line eval of the same checkpoint under BF16 vs NVFP4 inference (other angles).

hypotheses_assessed.hypothesis: H1: The quantized (4over6 NVFP4 experts) forward that the vLLM generator samples from is a weaker math solver than the BF16 model at the same weights, so the NVFP4 run starts with a lower reward/solve rate before RL has done anything.
hypotheses_assessed.reasoning: Both actors share one model_spec so rollouts are sampled from the quantized model (config_registry.py:798-803). At steps 1-3 (policy_version 0-2, lr 5e-7..1e-6) rewards are 0.078/0.047/0.016 vs 0.031/0.016/0.000; paired over steps 1-20 the deficit is +0.032 (t=3.70, 17/20 steps), over 1-30 +0.0385 (t=4.15, 24/30), 217 vs 143 correct of 1920 samples. Zero-std frac is already 0.76 vs 0.68 in steps 1-20. Conditional on BF16 difficulty bin, NVFP4 achieves ~0.6x in 1-100. Caveat: steps 1-10 alone are not significant (t=1.45), so the fixed-weights penalty is inferred from 20-30 steps during which ~20-30 tiny updates occurred; a checkpoint-level BF16-vs-NVFP4 inference eval is needed to nail the size.

hypotheses_assessed.hypothesis: H2: NVFP4 learns more slowly because fewer groups carry advantage signal (zero-std groups 0.70 vs 0.49) and 6% of its steps have zero gradient.
hypotheses_assessed.reasoning: Mechanism is real and quantified: 2.3-2.4 signal groups/step vs 2.9->4.1; 18 steps with grad_norm=0 vs 2; grad_norm tracks zero-std at r=-0.86. But it is downstream of H1 (the gap exists in steps 1-20) and cannot by itself explain a flat curve: BF16 also started at only 2.9 signal groups/step in block 1 and still climbed (reward slope t=9.7), whereas NVFP4 at 2.3 shows slope t=1.8. So reduced signal is an amplifier/consequence, not the root cause.

hypotheses_assessed.hypothesis: H3: The 4-6x larger trainer/generator logprob mismatch (k1 KL -0.0029 vs -0.0007 nats/token, worst-token 3.9 vs 1.1, 2.05% vs 0.32% tokens clipped) biases or nullifies the policy gradient enough to stall learning.

Against: per-step mismatch does not predict per-step reward inside the NVFP4 run (r=-0.005 mean, +0.04 clip), ratio_mean is 0.9991 (0.09% bias), clipped tokens are 2% and the clipped_frac counts zero-advantage tokens too (dapo.py:117-122), and only 7.7% more tokens differ bitwise (0.574 vs 0.533) -- the difference is in the tail, not the count. tfevents cannot tell whether a 2% clipped / 0.003-nat biased gradient is sufficient to stop learning; that requires a gradient-level experiment (e.g. train with BF16 rollouts + NVFP4 trainer, or NVFP4 rollouts + BF16 trainer).

angle: Direct checkpoint measurement: HF base weights (w0) vs step-300 DCP weights of arm_bf16_4x4_long and arm_nvfp4_deq_4x4_long — per-tensor drift, bf16-rounding changes, and NVFP4 4over6 code/scale changes using the real torchao quantizer.
summary: The step-300 checkpoints of BOTH runs are almost bitwise identical to the HF base: >99.2% of elements unchanged in every matrix, cosine(w0,w300)=1.000000, relative Frobenius drift 5e-5..2.6e-4, and no element with |w0| >= 2^-11 (4.88e-4) changed anywhere. Root reason (verified from the checkpoint metadata and code): both arms train in full bf16 — params AND AdamW moments are torch.bfloat16 (TrainingConfig(dtype="bfloat16") at experiments/rl/examples/alphabet_sort/config_registry.py:759, inherited by _ablation_base; configs.py:87-91 says this means no fp32 master copy), so the nominal AdamW step (p50 1.2e-7, max 9.5e-7 at lr 1e-6) is ~1000x smaller than the bf16 ulp of a median weight (0.0156 -> ulp 1.22e-4) and rounds to zero for >99.8% of elements; only near-zero weights (|w0| p50 ~1e-4) move, by up to ~300*lr = 2.5e-4. This contradicts the task premise of fp32 master weights and is a shared limitation of both arms, not a differentiator. Through the real 4over6 quantizer (1x16/mse/256, per-expert amax), quant(w300) differs from quant(w0) in only 0.017-0.043% of FP4 codes, <1e-6 of block scales, 0/128 expert amaxes, with identical 8.69% rel-RMS quantization error at w0 and w300 — for the BF16 run's weights as well as the NVFP4 run's. So the NVFP4 arm's forward/rollout consumed essentially the step-0 expert weights for all 300 steps, and the accumulated drift (rel 1e-4) is ~3 orders of magnitude below the per-forward NVFP4 quantization noise (rel 8.7e-2). Cross-run: the NVFP4 run drifted 20-26% less (rel-Fro 0.74-0.80x, exp_avg -22%, exp_avg_sq -34%, matching the logged grad-norm gap 0.12 vs 0.17), on largely the same near-zero elements (Jaccard 0.80-0.89) but with different values (identical on 3.3-3.5%, sign agreement 58-71%, drift cosine 0.66-0.72). The reward gap already exists in steps 1-20 (0.091 vs 0.059) when cumulative drift is <= 2e-5 on <1% of elements. Verdict for the user's question: the NVFP4 run did not fail to track BF16 because its weights learned differently — neither run's weights moved appreciably; the gap is a forward-pass (rollout + trainer forward) quantization-noise effect present from step 1, with a secondary weaker-gradient/less-drift effect downstream of the lower reward variance (more zero-std groups). Whether the BF16 run's own reward rise is caused by its ~1% near-zero-weight drift or by something else cannot be decided from checkpoints.

angle: Code-level trace of the NVFP4 (4over6, dequantized-backward) arm in trainer and generator + quantitative dead-zone estimate, verified against the real step-300 checkpoints of both runs
summary:
Within this angle the reward gap decomposes into one decisive, measured fact and one plausible-but-undecidable contributor.

DECISIVE (measured on the parked step-300 DCP checkpoints vs the HF init): BOTH runs train with bf16 master weights, not fp32 (TrainingConfig(dtype="bfloat16") in the shared base config; configs.py L87-91 documents "all parameters, gradients, and optimizer states in bfloat16, without an extra copy of fp32 weights"; DCP metadata dtype=torch.bfloat16 for params and Adam moments; 172 GiB = 6.0 B/param). At lr 1e-6 an Adam-normalized update (|update| <= ~lr) is below half a bf16 ulp for every element with |w| >= 2^-12 = 2.44e-4 (median expert |w| = 0.015, half-ulp 3.05e-5 = 30x lr), so it is rounded away every step with no residual. Result after 300 steps: 99.3% of expert-weight elements and ~99% of attention elements are bitwise identical to HF in BOTH arms; 98.6-99.4% of the elements that did change had |w_init| < 2.44e-4 (max 4.88e-4 = 2^-11); Adam exp_avg/exp_avg_sq are 100% nonzero, i.e. gradients arrived and were discarded at the bf16 store. The only learning channel in either arm is the ~0.9% of "tiny" elements.

That channel is what separates the arms. In the NVFP4 arm the 4over6 forward quantizes expert weights per expert (global amax) in 1x16 E2M1 blocks with E4M3 scales; the zero bin is |w| < block_amax/24 ~ 2e-3 (median block amax 0.046), so 100% of the tiny elements quantize to code 0 (simulated: tiny_frac_fp4_nonzero = 0.0). Quantizing the step-300 NVFP4 expert weights with a numpy reimplementation of the reference quantizer gives fp4 codes changed = 4.2e-7 (12 of 12,582,912 in the L12 w1 sample, all in ONE block whose 4/6 candidate flipped because a tiny neighbour moved; the block's non-tiny weights are bitwise unchanged), 0 expert amax changed. The fp4 expert operands that both the trainer forward and the vLLM generator compute with are therefore frozen at init for layers 0-39 (79.1% of params, ~45% of active FLOPs/token). The BF16 arm's 170M moved expert elements (0.70% of 24.2B) do enter its bf16 GEMMs. Counting changed elements the forward can see: BF16 ~206M vs NVFP4 ~34M (6x fewer; NVFP4's visible changes are only tail-layer experts, attention, router, embeddings, each also 4-15% smaller than BF16's).

This corrects the premise: the freeze is NOT the E2M1/E4M3 grid coarseness per se. With fp32 masters and consistent 1e-6/step updates (3e-4 after 300 steps) the simulation flips 11.9% of fp4 codes (4.3% at 1e-4) -- the fp4 forward would have moved. It is the bf16-master dead zone (shared by both arms) plus the fp4 zero bin swallowing the only movable elements (NVFP4-specific).

Trainer/generator consistency: the generator builds the same converted model_spec (only attention/GDN configs are replaced for vLLM), receives the trainer's bf16 weights uncast, and requantizes dynamically on every forward with the same code path and env knob; sampling policy == trainer policy up to kernel numerics.
